A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same FutureCAD research and contain 13 complete, readable pages, including Appendices A-D. Text, equations, tables, and figures support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original text-to-CAD generation, B-Rep grounding, and ablation results in Tables 1-3, with dataset analyses and failure examples in the appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains the original generation, grounding, and ablation experiments in Tables 1-3, together with the appendix analyses and examples.

M1.justification: Sections 3-5 retain the same CadQuery generation procedure, BRepGround architecture, supervised training, GSPO optimization, and geometric reward. No algorithmic component changes.

E1.justification: Both versions retain FutureCAD advanced and standard subsets, Fusion360 generalization evaluation, text-based B-Rep grounding, and the Appendix A dataset comparisons. No dataset or task coverage changes.

E2.justification: Tables 1-2 retain identical comparator membership: six generation baselines and LLM-Query, CLIP-DE, and Late Fusion for grounding. CADFusion and CAD-LLaMA remain the advanced-subset comparators; Appendix C is unchanged.

E3.justification: Section 6.1 and Appendices B-C retain the same splits, detailed-description inputs, training settings, metrics, baseline evaluation restrictions, 2,048-point CD computation, and advanced-feature validity protocol.

E4.justification: Table 3 retains the same SFT-only and without-BRepGround ablations. The generalization evaluation, Appendix A complexity analysis, and Appendix D failure cases are also unchanged.

E5.justification: Statistical reporting is unchanged. Neither version supplies experimental seed counts, repeated-run uncertainty, confidence intervals, or significance tests; the same aggregate performance metrics are reported.

E6.justification: All results in Tables 1-3 and Figures 4-7 are unchanged. For example, FutureCAD's advanced-subset invalidity remains 1.01%, and BRepGround's F1 remains 50.23%.

T1.justification: Equations (1)-(22), including feature-sequence definitions, execution dynamics, grounding formulations, training objectives, and baseline losses, are unchanged. No assumptions, derivations, or proofs are added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same claims about unifying program generation with B-Rep grounding, contributing over 140k CAD models, and achieving state-of-the-art generation and generalization.

C2.justification: Results interpretations in Sections 6.2-6.4 are unchanged. Appendix D retains the same explanations involving spatial reasoning, omitted refinements and class imbalance, and text-model inconsistency.

D1.justification: v1's introduction footnote promises future public release of data and code. v2 removes that promise and states in the abstract that code and dataset are available, providing a GitHub repository link. Other implementation and reproducibility details are unchanged.

R1.justification: Section 2, the references, and Appendix A retain the same cited works and positioning relative to parametric CAD generation, direct B-Rep modeling, and existing datasets.

P1.justification: v2 adds the availability sentence to the abstract, removes the future-release footnote, and updates the version and preprint dates. The remaining wording and section organization are preserved.

P2.justification: The abstract addition and footnote removal produce limited text reflow across pages 1-3; the Section 5.1 footnote is renumbered. All seven figures and three tables retain their content and design.

improvement.justification: Replacing a future-release promise with a concrete repository link modestly improves resource discoverability and reproducibility documentation. The scientific content and evidence are unchanged. The PDFs alone do not establish the linked resources' completeness or usability.
